What if the AI race isn't won by the smartest AI... but by the one that knows you best?
Meta looked like it was falling behind OpenAI, Google and Anthropic. So it started spending.
Around fourteen billion dollars for a huge stake in Scale AI, and its founder to lead a new lab: Meta Superintelligence Labs.
Giant pay offers to pull top researchers from rival labs.
Then the hardware. A data center in Ohio called Prometheus, built to reach a full gigawatt. An even bigger one in Louisiana called Hyperion.
Its own AI chips, called MTIA. And deals for nuclear power to keep it all running.
But here's the twist. Money and chips can be bought. Meta's real advantage can't.
Around three and a half billion people use its apps every day.
Twenty years of posts, likes, photos, friends, groups, and what you shop for.
Its tracking pixel follows activity on lots of other websites, too.
And now there are glasses with cameras, seeing the world from your eyes.
Your WhatsApp messages are end-to-end encrypted, so Meta can't read them. But it still knows a lot.
Search engines learn your questions. Chatbots learn your prompts. A social network learns your life.
So the scariest AI might not be the smartest one... it's the one that already knows you.
